chapter: Dizzy, Chano Pozo and Afro-Cuban jazz
title: Introducing Gillespie to conga rhythms
summary: He says he introduced Dizzy to the Afro-Cuban band sound and they recorded together.

blocks.x: Well, Gillespie was something else, because me and Gillespie played all the single work together we got. He was crazy with all that conga-bonga and all that kind of stuff.
Where did he get to hear it first?
(Inaudible) when he was goes with the band, I introduced that kind of music and that kind of a band, and we recorded publicly on this (inaudible).
The other day (inaudible) I read about (inaudible).
Because he made a thing called Conchita in 1941, which was a rhumba (inaudible).
And we (inaudible) on two numbers, and I forgot the name (inaudible). I can't find it.
Well, I went through his (inaudible), so I can check that out. I can check out the names of (inaudible).
All right. So naturally then (inaudible) I set up everything. And I went to the (inaudible) and got me a number of trumpet players, a record player, this and that, you know.
